Not strictly.

`ce-review` must run an obvious fast lint, typecheck, or focused test command and stop on failures unless conceptual review was requested ([SKILL.md](/Users/staggart/.agents/skills/ce-review/SKILL.md:86)).

But it may still finish—and even say `Ship it`—with tests “not run” when no focused command is found ([SKILL.md](/Users/staggart/.agents/skills/ce-review/SKILL.md:331)). So tests are part of the review, but a passing test run is not currently a hard verdict gate.

Yes—for TypeScript or React reviews, `ce-review` requires applying `code-taste` ([SKILL.md](/Users/staggart/.agents/skills/ce-review/SKILL.md:32)).

Pass 3 is explicitly the taste pass ([SKILL.md](/Users/staggart/.agents/skills/ce-review/SKILL.md:230)). It is integrated into the review, though not reported as a separately named “code-taste pass.” Python uses `spade-python-taste` instead.

I just ran a ce-review and it said of taste review:



> You’re right. I ran the code-taste pass, then incorrectly filtered its structural findings out because the functional bugs were higher severity. That made the “entire diff” review incomplete.



Like, how can I really enforce code taste as a requirement not a nice to have?

That is a real contract failure in `ce-review`, not reviewer discretion.

I’m using `prompt-check` to pin down the enforcement requirement, then checking the review synthesis rules and prior skill decisions.

The normalized requirement is: every applicable taste finding must survive synthesis unless it fails the evidence bar—not disappear because a higher-severity bug exists.

I’m tracing where the current review contract permits that loss.

content.text:
Make code taste a gate, not a lens. The current wording requires running it, but does not require its valid findings to survive synthesis.

Add this to `ce-review`:

```md
## Mandatory Taste Gate

For every TypeScript or React diff, run `code-taste` as an independent,
applicable pass.

Every taste finding that meets the shared evidence bar must appear in the final
review. Higher-severity findings may change ordering and verdict, but never
justify omitting taste findings.

A taste finding may be removed only when it is:
- a duplicate, in which case merge it into the retained finding;
- pre-existing and unaffected by the diff;
- unsupported by concrete code-path evidence; or
- preference-only with no maintenance consequence.

Do not emit the verdict until the taste pass is accounted for.
```

Then require this output:

```md
- Code taste: passed — no issues
- Code taste: completed — 3 findings reported
- Code taste: not applicable — no TypeScript or React changes
```

Also make `Ship it` unavailable when an applicable taste pass was not completed. Any retained `should-fix` taste finding already produces `Needs changes`.

That closes the actual loophole around synthesis in [ce-review](/Users/staggart/.agents/skills/ce-review/SKILL.md:286). It does not force fake findings when the code is clean.

# Response annotations:
Each item contains text selected from an earlier Codex response and may include a user comment. Treat items as Annotation 1, Annotation 2, and so on in array order. Use every selection as context and address every comment. For every annotation you address, include its inline directive `:codex-annotation{index="N"}`, where N is its one-based array position (for example, `:codex-annotation{index="1"}`). Do not use unstructured annotation labels.
<response-annotations>
[{"text":"Also make Ship it unavailable","annotation":"what makes it available?"}]
</response-annotations>

## My request:

Currently, `Ship it` is available when synthesis leaves no findings or only nits. There is no mechanical gate.

Add this verdict precondition:

> `Ship it` may be selected only when every applicable mandatory pass completed. For TypeScript or React diffs, this includes `code-taste`. Otherwise the verdict is `Review incomplete`.

:codex-annotation{index="1"}
ok can you make these adjustments please?
